instruction.text: You’re talking with a Victorian woman about her life. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: What was your life like at the beginning of the ((++Victorian Elizabethan)) era?
I used to live in a small ((++village car)) and work long hours on a farm.
Did your children go to school?
No, only children from ((poor ++rich)) families could go to school.
What did your children do then?
They worked dangerous ((++jobs parties)) to make money. My son went down the mines, and my daughter cleaned chimneys!

hint.label: Mines
hint.text: Mines are narrow tunnels that go deep underground and are dangerous places to work. During the Victorian era, people mostly mined coal.

instruction.text: Look at the images of life at the beginning and end of the Victorian era. How was life different by the end?

b.sound: The number of factories increased, and people moved to cities to work in them.
Most people continued to work on farms.

feedback.end: By the time Queen Victoria died, Britain was a completely different place compared to the start of her reign.

instruction.text: While factories became more popular to work at, there were lots of problems with them! Select the problems.

trainers.hint: More than one answer can be correct.

instruction.text: What do you think working in a Victorian factory would have been like?

feedback.end: Some of the most common dangers of working in factories included breaking your arm or being crushed if you got stuck in the machines!

instruction.text: There were lots of inventions during the Victorian era. Drag the inventions to the correct places on the timeline.

hint.label: Invention
hint.text: An invention is a new thing that someone has made.

instruction.text: Read the text about the different inventions and fill in the gaps.

feedback.finish: Other inventions, like cameras, also got better during the Victorian period. In fact, Queen Victoria was the first ever British monarch to be photographed!

atoms.b: The penny-farthing bicycle came along in 1871. It was famous for its two very ((++differently similarly)) sized wheels. The bicycle also had no ((handles ++brakes))!
Alexander Graham Bell invented the ((++telephone computer)) in 1876. It changed the world and made it possible to ((mindread ++talk_to)) people who were far away.
The ((++electric water)) light bulb was invented by Thomas Edison and Joseph Swan in 1879. It burned for a ((++longer shorter)) time than oil and gas lamps.
